name: LLM / AI-gateway usage governance
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Three architectural layers compete here and beava plays at the bottom layer. (a) Generic distributed-state substrate that almost every AI gateway uses for per-(api_key x model) TPM/RPM/$-spend counters: Redis is the overwhelming default (LiteLLM, Portkey, Kong AI, Tyk, agentgateway, Truefoundry all use Redis-or-DragonflyDB-or-Memcached for distributed rate-limit and virtual-key budget state); Postgres is the durable companion for cold storage and audit (a Redis-hot + Postgres-cold split is now the canonical pattern, with Portkey publicly documenting in-memory cache + Redis sync every 10s for budget increments); Cloudflare Durable Objects for serverless-edge deployments. (b) In-process Go/Rust counters for single-replica deploys (Bifrost ~11 microseconds at 5k RPS, Helicone <5ms p95 in Rust pre-Mintlify-acquisition, Envoy AI Gateway 1-3ms via Envoy Global Rate Limit API). (c) Stream-processing / feature-store substrate (Flink, Materialize, RisingWave, Tecton-now-Databricks, Hopsworks, Chalk, Feast) only shows up at large enterprises that already have a Kafka pipeline feeding their AI-platform analytics - none of these have shipped LLM-gateway-specific reference integrations as of 2026 and the latency profile (10s of ms with broker hop) is wrong for inline gateway decisions. Beava competes at layer (a) by collapsing the Redis-hot + Postgres-cold substrate into a single Apache-2.0 binary that speaks the per-(key x model x tenant x agent) primitives natively rather than as Redis key-naming conventions. Crucially, NO AI gateway today uses a streaming feature server for inline TPM/RPM enforcement - the segment is a Redis monoculture with an open architectural seam.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Standalone OSS AI gateways (each ships built-in TPM/RPM/budget/abuse features): Portkey (Apache-2.0 gateway open-sourced fully March 2026, $15M Series A Feb 19 2026 led by Elevation Capital with Lightspeed participation, 2 trillion tokens/day, $1M+ spend/day, 24,000 organizations, 125M req/day, 10.9k stars, Postman/Snorkel AI as named customers, governance-for-agentic-AI is the explicit funding-cycle priority); LiteLLM/BerriAI (45k+ GitHub stars and dominant Python proxy, but suffered a high-profile dual blow in March 2026 - supply-chain compromise of PyPI packages v1.82.7/1.82.8 affecting 95M monthly downloads on March 24, plus CVE-2026-42208 SQL injection in the authentication path exploited within 36 hours of disclosure, plus the Delve fake-SOC2 scandal that exposed the certification chain - reputation damage in the enterprise segment is real and ongoing); Helicone (YC W23, acquired by Mintlify March 3 2026 and shifted to maintenance mode with managed migrations off the platform - this removed the strongest sub-5ms Rust competitor from the market and customers are actively shopping for alternatives, 14.2 trillion tokens cumulative through 16,000 orgs); Bifrost/Maxim AI (Go, Apache-2.0, 11 microsecond overhead at 5k RPS, MCP-native, ~4.9k stars, Maxim AI commercial overlay); Truefoundry ($19M Series A led by Intel Capital with Peak XV / Eniac / Jump Capital, named in Gartner 10 Best Practices for Optimizing Generative & Agentic AI Costs 2026, 4x YoY customer growth, Siemens Healthineers / Resmed / Automation Anywhere / NVIDIA / Games 24x7 as customers, SOC2/HIPAA/ITAR-compliant, MCP Gateway claims 99% token savings); agentgateway/Solo.io (Apache-2.0, v1.0 in 2026, MCP+A2A+Kubernetes Gateway API native, explicit local-vs-global rate-limit distinction with Redis-backed global mode, CEL-descriptor per-tool rate limits); Requesty (EU-compliant routing); TensorZero; LLMGateway.io. Hyperscaler / proxy-vendor AI gateways: Cloudflare AI Gateway (free baseline tier, 10-50ms overhead, daily/weekly/monthly spend caps, 2026 unified-billing feature where you pay third-party model usage on your Cloudflare invoice, bundled into Workers); Envoy AI Gateway (Tetrate + Bloomberg, Apache-2.0, CNCF Envoy Gateway-based, v0.1 Feb 25 2025, token-based rate limit via Envoy Global Rate Limit API, 1-3ms overhead, FIPS-verified Tetrate Enterprise Gateway distribution); Kong AI Gateway (AI Rate Limiting Advanced plugin is enterprise-only, 2026 release introduces model-based limits replacing provider-based, integrated with OPA, 2-5ms overhead); Apigee LLMTokenQuota / PromptTokenLimit policies + Model Armor (scattered policy approach, criticized vs purpose-built gateways); Tyk AI Studio (multi-vendor routing, token-level metering with team/project/app attribution); Zuplo AI Gateway (edge, 300+ data centers, hierarchical cost budgets, semantic caching, prompt-injection detection); KrakenD; Traefik Hub. MCP gateways: MintMCP (SOC 2 Type II, purpose-built for regulated industries), Composio (850+ pre-built connectors), agentgateway, Lasso Security (security-first with PI detection + server reputation), Splunk MCP Server (beta). Agent-observability with cost / step tracking: LangSmith (LangChain), AgentOps (400+ LLMs, 25x fine-tuning cost reduction claim), Galileo, Arize, Langfuse (acquired by ClickHouse January 2026 alongside ClickHouse's $400M Series D - removes another OSS observability incumbent into a hyperscaler-data-platform fold), Langwatch, Datadog LLM Observability, OpenLLMetry/Traceloop. Guardrail/safety vendors that consume velocity signal: Lakera, Protect AI, Prompt Security, HiddenLayer, Robust Intelligence, NeMo Guardrails, AWS Bedrock Guardrails, Azure AI Content Safety, Snowflake Cortex Guardrails. M&A theme of 2026: incumbents are getting absorbed (Helicone -> Mintlify, Langfuse -> ClickHouse), the standalone-gateway segment is consolidating, and the Portkey Apache-2.0 turn is a defensive move against the consolidation.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Apache-2.0 is now the dominant license posture across the OSS gateway segment - a friendlier license environment than fraud / AML / payments where BSL and proprietary dominate. Portkey gateway is Apache-2.0 (fully open-sourced March 2026, previously source-available with restrictions - the relicense is a recent and meaningful signal that the segment is competing on license openness, not protecting closed cores); LiteLLM is MIT (most permissive); Bifrost is Apache-2.0; agentgateway is Apache-2.0; Envoy AI Gateway is Apache-2.0 (CNCF, double-stamped via Envoy Gateway lineage); Helicone was Apache-2.0 pre-Mintlify-acquisition and remains so in maintenance mode. The control-plane / hosted analytics layer is closed-source for nearly all OSS gateways (Portkey's hosted control plane is closed, LiteLLM Enterprise is paid, Helicone Cloud was paid pre-acquisition, Bifrost Maxim platform is paid, Truefoundry is proprietary) - this open-core split is structural to the segment but the OSS gateway itself ships Apache-2.0 with full TPM/RPM/budget on-day-one. Proprietary closed-source incumbents: Truefoundry, Kong AI Gateway Enterprise plugins, Apigee, Tyk core, Zuplo, Cloudflare AI Gateway, MintMCP, all hyperscaler AI gateways. Notable shifts in 2026: Redis itself remains under the post-AGPLv3/SSPL relicense and Valkey (Apache-licensed in spirit, BSD-3-Clause technically) is the cloud-default replacement that ships as the redis package in Ubuntu 26.04 - AI-gateway vendors who pinned to Redis are now defaulting to Valkey for new deployments, which removes 'Redis license risk' as a wedge but reinforces the Apache-substrate expectation. Beava's Apache-2.0 with no open-core split is therefore a credible posture in this segment but NOT differentiating on its own - the wedge has to be technical (sub-ms inline, primitive-rich) because the license bar is met by competitors. Where Apache-2.0 does materially help is for AI-gateway vendors who would EMBED beava as a feature substrate inside their closed-source product or behind their managed control plane - they can ship Apache-2.0 internally without GPL contamination concerns; Jube (AGPL-3.0) and BSL competitors fail that test, beava passes it.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High and rising fast - one of the most bundling-pressured segments in the entire beava market map. Three vectors are real and active in 2026: (1) Cloudflare AI Gateway is FREE on the baseline tier, bundled into the Workers subscription any Cloudflare customer already pays for, and the March 2026 unified-billing feature lets buyers pay third-party model usage (OpenAI, Anthropic) directly on the Cloudflare invoice with a small convenience fee - this removes the AI-gateway procurement decision entirely for any buyer already on Cloudflare, even though it costs the 10-50ms proxy hop; (2) AWS Bedrock Guardrails + Azure AI Content Safety + Google Vertex AI both ship request-level guardrails, content filters, denied topics, and per-deployment rate limits bundled into their respective model APIs - the buyer who is single-cloud and single-provider gets 'good enough' governance for free; (3) Databricks (with Tecton + Fennel acquired in 2025) and Snowflake (with Cortex Guardrails) now offer LLM serving + guardrails + cost-attribution inside the same platform a buyer already runs their data warehouse on, with the Tecton sub-ms feature-server claim (0.8ms) directly threatening beava's latency wedge for any buyer in the Databricks orbit. The mitigating factor: hyperscaler bundles each cover ONE provider's traffic, NOT the multi-provider routing that is the entire point of an AI gateway - Portkey routes 1,600+ models across 250+ providers, LiteLLM routes 100+, Bifrost 1,000+, and that multi-provider story is the wedge against hyperscaler bundles. A buyer who is locked into Bedrock-only or Azure-OpenAI-only is hyperscaler-bundled regardless. A buyer running OpenAI + Anthropic + Bedrock + Vertex + Together + Fireworks + Groq + on-prem fine-tunes can never use a single hyperscaler bundle and needs a real AI gateway, and that gateway needs a real feature substrate. Beava's wedge survives in the multi-provider buyer segment; the single-provider segment is lost to the hyperscaler.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Excellent fit shape - this segment is the one where beava's HTTP/TCP-push model is closest to native. AI gateways already emit per-call request/response events over HTTP/JSON or callbacks/hooks, not Kafka, so the Kafka-shaped friction that hurts beava in AML (V7) and fraud (V1) is materially absent here. Producers (AI gateways emitting per-call events): LiteLLM (Python proxy, OpenAI-format, virtual keys, custom callbacks/handlers, integration via thin plugin); Portkey Gateway (TypeScript/Node, plugin/hook architecture, OpenAI-compatible REST, 1,600+ model variants from 250+ providers); Bifrost (Go, plugin SDK, native MCP); Truefoundry (Node.js backend, MCP+Agent+LLM gateway trio); agentgateway (Rust, MCP+A2A+Kubernetes Gateway API); Kong AI Gateway (OpenResty + Lua plugins, ai-rate-limiting-advanced plugin point); Envoy AI Gateway (Wasm filters or ext_proc, Envoy Global Rate Limit API integration is the canonical pattern); Apigee policy chain (LLMTokenQuota / PromptTokenLimit / SemanticCacheLookup); Tyk AI Studio; Zuplo Workers; KrakenD; Cloudflare AI Gateway (Workers RPC). MCP-specific producers: MintMCP, Composio, agentgateway, Lasso, Splunk MCP. Agent SDK callbacks: LangChain / LangGraph callbacks, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic Computer Use SDK, AutoGen, CrewAI, Pydantic AI. OpenTelemetry-based producers: OpenLLMetry / Traceloop, Datadog LLM Observability, MLflow AI Monitoring, Langfuse (post-ClickHouse), AgentOps - any of these can fan out to beava as a second sink via OTLP-to-beava adapter. Concretely: a thin Python or TypeScript plugin (a few hundred lines) that pushes llm_request / llm_response / tool_call events to beava via TCP+msgpack and pulls per-(api_key x model) TPM/RPM/$-spend / per-agent step counters via batch_get is the canonical integration shape - this maps directly to what LiteLLM, Portkey, Helicone-pre-Mintlify, agentgateway already do against Redis today, with beava as a drop-in Apache-2.0 substrate. The single biggest missing connector is a Rust/Go client SDK - AI gateways are mostly written in Go (Bifrost, agentgateway) or Rust (Helicone, parts of others); a Python-only SDK constrains beava to the LiteLLM-and-ML-platform-team niche.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, but lean toward rules engine. The dominant pattern in this market is a deterministic rules layer (per-key TPM < X; per-agent identical_tool_calls_60s < Y; per-tenant $-spend/hour < $Z; per-(api_key x model) cap; budget hierarchy Customer -> Team -> Virtual Key -> Provider Config) combined with an optional ML/classifier scorer for jailbreak/prompt-injection scoring (Lakera, Prompt Security, NeMo Guardrails, AWS Bedrock Guardrails). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled - the gateway implements the rule with batch_get + comparison, and the classifier reads the same features as side input. The four-tier budget hierarchy is a concrete pattern this segment converges on (e.g., Portkey, Truefoundry, LiteLLM) and beava's composite-key @bv.table model maps onto it naturally. Beava is feature-only and never the policy engine, which matches how Helicone, Portkey, Bifrost, Truefoundry, agentgateway all separate 'metering + counters' from 'policy + enforcement'. The natural beava positioning is invisible substrate inside an AI-gateway product - the buyer never sees beava, they see the gateway's budget-controls UI and the budget UI reads from beava.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Six concrete reasons an AI-gateway vendor or AI-platform-engineering team would pick beava over Redis or in-process Go/Rust counters: (1) Primitives mapping is exact. The per-(api_key x model) TPM, per-(tenant x team) $-spend, per-agent identical-tool-call counter, per-(api_key x rule_id) jailbreak-family velocity are literally what beava's ~60 aggregation primitives express in 1-2 line @bv.event / @bv.table declarations; competitors hand-roll these in 10+ line Redis-Lua scripts or in-process Go counters that don't survive replica scale-out. The agentgateway team explicitly documents 'local' (per-replica in-process) vs 'global' (Redis-backed) rate-limit because cluster-wide quota coordination matters and Redis is the only option today - beava is a third option that is both globally consistent AND sub-ms. (2) Latency budget fit. Inline AI-gateway decision budget is <5ms p99 (Helicone <5ms, Truefoundry <5ms, Envoy 1-3ms, Bifrost 11 microseconds, Kong 2-5ms); beava's TCP+msgpack get / batch_get is inside that envelope when co-located, vs Redis-Lua at ~1ms RTT plus the Lua-script latency or Postgres at 5-20ms which is below the budget. The hyperscaler-bundled Cloudflare AI Gateway at 10-50ms is the bottom of the latency tier and beava is at the top. (3) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split. Matches what AI-gateway vendors WANT to embed - Portkey gateway (Apache-2.0 since March 2026), Bifrost (Apache-2.0), agentgateway (Apache-2.0), Envoy AI Gateway (Apache-2.0 via CNCF) all explicitly chose Apache to attract vendor adoption; beava fits the same posture and is one of the few feature-substrate options that does NOT carry AGPL (Jube) or post-relicense (Redis-the-product, though Valkey solves this) baggage. AI-gateway vendors who would embed a feature substrate across many bank/SaaS tenants need Apache-2.0 for closed-source distribution. (4) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster. Matches the topology this market converges on: one Helicone-pre-acquisition / Bifrost / agentgateway binary per cluster or per pod; beava as a sidecar adds one binary, not a stack. (5) Push-on-event model. AI gateways already emit per-call request/response events over HTTP/JSON or callbacks; no Kafka hop is needed, which is why competitors use Redis directly today - beava preserves that topology while replacing the Redis-Lua complexity with a typed primitive surface. (6) Composite-key cross-products as first-class. (api_key x model), (tenant x user), (agent_id x tool_name), (api_key x rule_id) are first-class @bv.table grain in beava; in Redis they are key-naming conventions with no schema enforcement, and in Postgres they are joins that don't fit the latency budget. The single most underrated wedge: per-entity feature vectors with 20-60 features each fit beava's batch_get exactly - competitors burn 10+ Redis round-trips per inline decision or write unsafe Lua mega-scripts. Underlying these wedges is a market timing observation: with Helicone exiting to Mintlify (March 2026), LiteLLM compromised (March 2026 supply-chain attack + Delve SOC2 scandal), Langfuse exiting to ClickHouse (January 2026), and Portkey explicitly raising $15M Feb 2026 to build a 'governance layer with permissions, identity, access boundaries, and budget guardrails' for agentic AI, the substrate layer underneath agentic-AI governance is being rebuilt in 2026 - there is a genuine window for an Apache-2.0 single-binary substrate with the right primitives to enter the conversation.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking AI-gateway deployment today (derived from use case 16's open_engineering_gaps and SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md v0 invariants), in priority order: (1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 in v0 - disqualifying for any deployment where the AI gateway and feature backend are not in the same trust domain. Every named competitor in this segment ships mTLS / API-key / OAuth / JWT on day one (Portkey, LiteLLM-pre-CVE, Helicone, Bifrost, Truefoundry, agentgateway). This is the single biggest blocker and explicitly worse here than for fraud (V1) because AI-gateway buyers include security-conscious enterprises and post-LiteLLM-CVE-2026-42208 the segment is hyperattentive to auth-path attacks. (2) No in-process sharding - caps single-tenant scale at one node, a hyperscale AI-gateway vendor running multi-million-tenant SaaS (Portkey serves 24,000 orgs, Helicone served 16,000) cannot horizontally scale within one beava cluster. (3) No cross-node feature replication / merge / CRDT counters - competing AI gateways use Redis precisely so their TPM / RPM counters are cluster-consistent across N gateway replicas (agentgateway explicitly documents the consistency trade-off, Portkey publicly describes in-memory + Redis-sync-every-10s for budget increments). Without a 'global mode', beava is a single-replica solution in a multi-replica gateway-deployment world, which is the default at every named buyer. (4) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' - runaway-agent kill-switches and adaptive provider-aware throttling want event-driven hooks ('when (agent_id).identical_tool_calls_60s > 50, fire webhook to kill session'); the $47k LangChain runaway-loop case study is the canonical demand driver and polling with batch_get on the hot path adds avoidable round-trips. Competing AI gateways already implement this as webhooks (Portkey alerts, Truefoundry budget alerts, Helicone alerts). (5) No multi-tenancy primitives - per-tenant namespaces, per-tenant quotas on the admin surface, per-tenant isolation; AI-gateway vendors serving many customers need this on day one (Truefoundry, Portkey, Helicone all ship multi-tenant native). (6) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS - billing-grade per-tenant cost meters that need calendar-month or 6-month retention must export to an external store; beava is the wrong place for the EU AI Act Article 12 audit retention obligation (Aug 2 2026, 6 months minimum, up to EUR 15M or 3% global turnover penalty). (7) No Rust / Go / TypeScript / Java client SDKs - the AI-gateway buyer ecosystem is in Go (Bifrost, agentgateway), Rust (Helicone), TypeScript (Portkey, MCP gateways), and Python (LiteLLM, Truefoundry partially). Wire is language-agnostic; SDK matrix is the gap. (8) No first-class HLL / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives prominently documented - explosive session / trace cardinality (10M+ session_ids / day at mid-size buyers) and 'top-k tenants by $-spend last 5 min' FinOps queries need approximate aggregates with bounded memory. (9) No tumbling-window primitives aligned to calendar boundaries (per-minute / per-hour / per-day) - provider-side TPM is rolling-60-second so a 1m sliding sum is needed, but billing-grade per-tenant cost meters and provider-billing-period accounting want calendar-aligned tumbling; beava ships sliding only. (10) No idempotency-on-request_id (exactly-once writes) - the same counter is reused for billing-adjacent accounting and double-counting biases velocity upward (acceptable for abuse signal) but breaks billing-grade $-spend (not acceptable for FinOps). (11) No first-class embedding-distance / cosine-similarity primitive - jailbreak-similarity detection (distance(prompt_embedding, known_jailbreak_centroid)) is best done with cosine-similarity in a vector index; beava can store the precomputed score but the buyer with a 'detect jailbreak families via embedding distance' requirement will look elsewhere. [uncertain] (12) No streaming admin / debug surface ('top-k api_keys by guardrail_hit_rate last 5 min', 'top-k agents by tool_call rate') - SOC / safety analysts need this for incident response and FinOps needs 'top-k tenants by $-spend last hour' for the dashboard. (13) No audit / structured log of admin writes for SOC 2 and EU AI Act Article 12 - even if beava is not the audit store, its own admin plane needs to be auditable.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 3-6mo for an AI-gateway-vendor embed deal (the lowest-friction path - the vendor handles security perimeter, auth, multi-tenancy at the gateway layer and beava is invisible substrate underneath; the must-have list collapses to TLS+auth on the admin port + idempotency-on-request_id + a Rust or Go SDK + at least one published reference integration with LiteLLM / Portkey / Bifrost / agentgateway). 6-12mo for direct sale to an AI-platform-engineering team at an enterprise building in-house (must additionally ship per-tenant namespaces, cross-node global mode with Redis-or-CRDT semantics, triggers/webhooks, calendar-aligned tumbling windows, HLL/CMS/Top-K primitives prominently documented). 12mo+ for the hyperscale segment (Cloudflare AI Gateway, OpenAI gateway-side enforcement) which needs in-process sharding, multi-region active-active, and SOC2 Type II - this segment is also where hyperscaler bundling is strongest and the GTM cost is highest, so it should not be the wedge target. The opportunistic path is the embed deal: post-Helicone-acquisition (March 2026) the segment has a vacancy at the 'sub-5ms Rust/Go OSS substrate' tier, and Portkey's $15M Series A explicitly targets the governance layer for agentic AI - both are credible design partners for a 3-6 month integration.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Zero published external proof points for beava in this segment, with caveats. Beava-side: no publicly named users in AI-gateway / agent-quota deployments located in use case 16 deep research; no Helicone/Portkey/LiteLLM/Bifrost/agentgateway integration in beava's repo; no LLM-vertical demo at /python/beava/demos (only adtech/ecommerce/fraud); no AI-gateway-shaped workload in crates/beava-bench/; no AI-gateway-shaped acceptance test in python/tests/v0; no LLM-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion / RFC threads located. Beava knows roughly who the buyer is (AI-gateway vendor wanting to embed a feature substrate, AI-platform-engineering team building in-house) and has the technical fit on paper. Competitor-side validation that the segment shape and demand are very real and growing fast: Portkey at 2 trillion tokens/day, $1M+ LLM spend/day, 24,000 organizations, 125M req/day, $15M Series A Feb 2026; Helicone at 14.2 trillion tokens cumulative through 16,000 orgs pre-Mintlify acquisition; LiteLLM at 45k+ GitHub stars and 95M monthly downloads pre-CVE; Truefoundry $19M Series A, 4x YoY customer growth, named in Gartner's '10 Best Practices for Optimizing Generative & Agentic AI Costs 2026', Siemens Healthineers / Resmed / NVIDIA as customers; Bifrost ~4.9k stars and 11 microsecond benchmark; agentgateway v1.0 in 2026 with explicit MCP/A2A/Kubernetes Gateway API native posture; Envoy AI Gateway built by Tetrate + Bloomberg with Apache-2.0 CNCF lineage. Market scale signals (also cited in use case 16): LLM Middleware Gateway $18.9M (2026) to $189M (2034), 49.6% CAGR per Intel Market Research; Enterprise LLM $5.91B (2026) to $48.25B (2034), 30% CAGR per Fortune Business Insights; ~80% of enterprises expected to have deployed generative AI APIs by end of 2026; ~42% of enterprises already using a middleware/gateway layer. Urgency drivers in 2026 are specific and dated: the $47k LangChain agent-loop incident (real, well-documented, 11-day runaway, became a canonical training example by March 2026 with multiple DEV.to/Medium/HN postmortems); the LiteLLM supply-chain compromise (March 24 2026, CVE-2026-42208 SQL injection in auth path within 36 hours, Delve fake-SOC2 scandal); EU AI Act Article 12 logging obligations effective August 2 2026 with 6-month retention minimum and penalties up to EUR 15M / 3% global turnover; OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 (LLM01 Prompt Injection appears in 73% of production AI deployments per 2026 audits, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption explicit); MCP rate-limit standardization across MintMCP / Composio / agentgateway / Lasso / Splunk MCP. Repo-side evidence of beava match is weaker than for fraud (V1) - no demo, no acceptance test, no published integration. The gap between segment urgency (very high) and beava proof-points (zero) is the largest in the entire market-position map - this is the strongest 'segment ready and waiting' / 'beava silent' contrast. evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Lead - LLM/AI-gateway usage governance is the strongest brand-new segment fit for beava in 2026 and the one with the most favorable market timing. Three converging signals make this a Lead-class call: (a) Segment is genuinely new (incumbents <2y old: Portkey founded 2023, Helicone YC W23, Bifrost 2024, agentgateway 2025), the Redis-Lua monoculture is the architectural seam, and no streaming feature server has shipped a reference integration yet - first-mover real estate is open. (b) Market is in active consolidation in 2026 (Helicone -> Mintlify March 2026 maintenance-mode, Langfuse -> ClickHouse January 2026, LiteLLM compromised March 2026, Portkey $15M Series A Feb 2026 explicitly for agentic-AI governance) - buyers are shopping for substrate and the post-Helicone vacancy at the 'sub-5ms Rust/Go OSS substrate' tier is a concrete inbound. (c) Demand drivers are specific and dated (EU AI Act Article 12 Aug 2 2026, $47k LangChain runaway-loop case study, OWASP LLM10 unbounded consumption framing, MCP rate-limit standardization) and the urgency wave is happening NOW, not in a 2027-2028 horizon. Recommended go-to-market is the embed path, not the direct-sale path: pick one OSS gateway vendor (Portkey, Bifrost, agentgateway are best technical fits and Apache-2.0-compatible) and offer to be the feature substrate behind their virtual-key budget / per-tenant TPM / per-agent step-counter layer. Engineering scope is 3-6 months focused on TLS+auth+global-mode+triggers+Rust/Go SDK+idempotency, and procurement timeline is the vendor's (much shorter than tier-1 bank cycles). The risk to a Lead call is that the hyperscaler bundle (Cloudflare AI Gateway / Bedrock / Azure / Vertex / Databricks-Tecton) eats the bottom of the market and the segment compresses faster than expected - but the multi-provider routing requirement insulates the substrate decision and the Apache-2.0 OSS gateway tier appears stable. Ship a runnable demo ('@bv.event llm_request' + '@bv.table per_key_tpm' + '@bv.event guardrail_hit' + 'shut down a $47k runaway agent in 8 seconds') as the first artifact; that single demo would address the 'repo evidence absent' gap and unlock at least one design-partner conversation.
